source: Although my sister Margaret of Austria is dead, you will stay with her nephew, at her court.
You will assume a new name and a new title. You will not speak of your old life.
And you will go alone, in a carriage I arrange for you in utmost privacy. Do you understand?
O-Oh, my God.
You're-- you want me to-- leave Denmark forever?
Now you understand.
I don't, though. Why are you doing this for me?
This can never be a world worth living in if women don't protect one another.
Men will sell us, breed us, hit us, dishonor us, and kill us. They rend us apart the moment they're born from us.
Someday there will be a young girl in your care suffering the way you've suffered recently.
And you must protect her life with your last breath. Do you understand?
I do.
Now get up.
I have one final command to you, as your Queen and the lady you serve.
Never return to Denmark. Never write to your father or your mother. Never think of the life you had.
My lady, I would honor this request outright, but I have promised your husband some proof.
Especially in light of your request that Lady Birgitta be executed in a hidden place, rather than in public.
I see. My husband knows my true character. He likely suspects me of something like this.
Will cutting off a hand do?
I think that should suffice, yes.
You're going to take off my hand?
Would you rather it was your head?
Cut away, then.
Just, please, not my left hand. That's the one I hold a brush in.
The right hand it is, then. The flesh on your wrist must be singed to stop the bleed. And Her Majesty and Lady Ophelia need not be present.
All of us shall agree to never speak of this incident. Isn't that right, Ophelia?
If that's what the Queen wants.
Of course. My eternal thanks, Ophelia, Bernardo.
Today, Brit is dead.
I don't know how to repay you, my lady.
I was so cruel to you. And to everyone. I followed Fortinbras' commands. I can never change that.
You were a child in the middle of war. Go, and join no more battles.
Go, and live.
I shall be brief with the cutting, and use a sharp axe.
Come with me.
Please, Bernardo, will you do me one kindness? Will you write my mother?
Will you tell her I love her, now and forever?
Kindness is a virtue not normally afforded to traitors.
But, yes. I will promise you that one small thing.
Thank you. Thank you. Goodbye, the both of you. And get on with it.
It is you. Excellent.
No! This shouldn't be happening! I—
I did not intend to trouble you, lady.
What are you doing out here?
Commending you for your most excellent performance. I've heard Lady Brit was apprehended for her, mm, shall we say, aspirations.
I'd like to trim the fat from this act, as it were. Cut straight to the action. Reduce the tedium.
I find repetition in plays absolutely boring. I've even been known to walk out at the intermission!
What are you talking about?
What was once canonical can be rewritten.
Take my word for it that Lady Brit will never trouble you again.
The dangling plot thread is, shall we say, snipped.
I look forward to seeing what tomorrow brings. It will be a refreshing change of pace for both actor and audience, I think.
Farewell, my lady! Adieu!
Does this mean I'm free of all this? Of this repeating world? And I'll move forward with the rest of my life now?
That nightmare I had—it didn't end when Hamlet killed my father.
I also saw the King and Queen dead. I saw my brother murder Hamlet.
Does that mean... that's what's coming for me? And they're all going to die, all of them?
Oh, my dear. You know, the weather is quite wonderful in Elsinore this time of year!
Do try to enjoy the next day fully. One mustn't trouble oneself with the future until it has come to pass.
Strange, as usual.
He's clearly trapped outside the flow of time, like me. But... in a different sort of way. More powerful.
I can use him to my advantage. He seems to know more about my situation than he lets on.
Brit, please tell me everything I've heard is untrue.
I heard you have been passing information to Norway.
This is ridiculous, right? It's not true, is it?
It's true.
Then why? Why would you do it?
Listen closely.
I last began passing information to Fortinbras by way of my father several months ago. It's why I was sent to Elsinore.
The other nobles, including my father, wanted Claudius dead. He was a poor King.
He disregarded all advice and requests which came his way. He ignored my father.
And to ignore powerful men is to wish for one's own death.
And then I found you. And your father. And you knew so much. You're a startlingly perceptive man.
I... see.
So you were using me for information.
No! No, I wasn't! Listen, Laertes: I love you.
But a coup is what the country needs. I truly believe it in my heart. Denmark deserves a better King.
If my father succeeds in helping Norway overthrow the throne, then the whole bad tree be uprooted. You see?
And with all these vile men dead and gone, you and I would remain to love in peace.
There would no longer be anyone to stop us. You see?
I do see.
I see that I was the more deceived.
I've been passing information from my father to you in confidence for months.
You're saying all of that went right to Norway?
Even if you intended to keep me alive, do you really believe Norway would stage a coup without bloodshed?
What about my sister? She's clearly terrified. She thinks someone's after her. Was that your doing, too?
She's not wrong. It was me.
But I had no choice. Fortinbras and my father came up with this plan.
Then why weren't you honest with me? We could have uncovered a solution together!
I was afraid.
I didn't truly believe I could trust you.
It's been discussed. Her death would have put many things in motion.
But no. I couldn't. I wouldn't. She's done nothing to deserve it.
Well, in the end, that's not what's important.
You lied to me and used me. That's as much as I need to know.
Bernardo, you may come in now. I had hoped to prove her innocence, but I believe you heard everything you needed to hear.
I'm here to escort you to the dungeon until we're able to thoroughly investigate your confession, my lady.
And my men will be looking through your personal effects.
Then this is to be the end of me.
So be it. I knew this might happen.
I wished with all my heart that things could have been different.
And for what little it's worth, Laertes, I am truly, abysmally sorry.
You're right. That's worth nothing at all.
Please. Listen.
Lord Laertes.
I don't know why I bothered to come. I have nothing to say to you.
Then go.
No. Actually, there's one thing. Bernardo tells me you wanted to have my sister murdered.
I didn't know.
I didn't know she was my target. Not until very recently.
And then, I didn't want to kill her. I fought. But...
You fought? But you still meant to go through with it? You still meant to kill Ophelia?
I don't know.
You're a liar, a murderer, and a traitor to everyone in this castle who knew you.
Please, God, leave, Laertes. Please. Just have mercy. I'll be dead soon. Then you never have to look at me again.
It may not make sense now, or ever, but I'm sorry I deceived you. Everything I felt for you was honest. I love you more than anyone in the world.
But I didn't have a choice about your sister. I never did. My whole life was—
No more. I don't care.
I shouldn't have come here.
I hope you go to Hell for threatening my sister.
And for using me.
Oh, God, I'm so scared.
You're here?
I came home early, Father. Never mind the details. Look at you. What have they done to you?
They arrested you for treason? Truly?
I can't believe they would do this to you. After all you've done for this court.
It is not unusual for royalty to turn on those who serve them.
And... there are things you don't know about my history with this court. About my service to King Hamlet.
I suppose it was only a matter of time until that past came back to haunt me.
But Father, you aren't a threat to anyone. This is merely meant to make an insult of you. Of us.
And I won't allow it.
Don't act in haste, Laertes.
You mean as they did with you? With this mockery of justice?
Claudius must be punished for this. He must know that he's crossed a line. And I will be the one to make him understand.
The rest of the castle needs to know what happens when they cross a line with us. I will be the one to make them understand.
I know I cannot stop you. So please-- just be safe.
I'll do my best. Farewell for now, Father. You'll be free soon enough.
My poor son. He knows not what he does.
Hamlet mentioned I could meet the ghost here.
But it doesn't look like that's true.
Hamlet said I could meet the ghost on the walls at midnight.
It's nearly time now.
Go to the walls?

source: Not right now. I've more important things than ghost hunting.
Luckily, I arrived early.
Things are almost peaceful, here at the start of it all.
You and I are the only ones who know about what's coming for them. The rest of them—they'll never believe me, will they?
It is impossible, yes. It is the rules of the larger game.
This is a game to you?
I did not give it that name. But it is a game all the same, and you the one forecasted to lose.
Now then. What news do you bring?
Death becomes you.
And you as well, clearly.
Be wary of every familiar face.
One of them will betray you.
Who? If you know, why won't you tell me?
Would that I could. But I am unable, through no law of my own.
I'm sure you'll find out soon enough.
I see one of your compatriots has had you killed.
Welcome to the ranks of the famous and esteemed. Those who die before their time live on in memory longer.
Though yours is a more heroic fate than dying on your stomach in the garden.
Of course, they will find your waterlogged corpse in the pond and say you drowned...
Leaving out the gash in your neck when they tell the tale.
They'd lie about why I died? Why?
Because a gash on an innocent maiden defies explanation. Suicide is a story easily told.
There has to be a way around it. So far as there always has been.
Yes. There is. Your killer may be known to you, as mine was.
